finalText:
Both combine the changes from one branch into another, but they handle history differently.

**Merge** adds a new commit that ties two histories together. Nothing gets rewritten, so it's safe on shared branches, but you end up with an extra "merge commit" and a history that shows every side branch.

**Rebase** replays your commits on top of another branch, one by one. History stays a straight line, but it rewrites commit hashes. That's fine on your own unpushed work, risky on anything others have already pulled.

Rule of thumb: rebase your local feature branch to keep history clean before sharing it, merge when bringing finished work into a shared branch like `main`.
